sources.title: ArcelorMittal to halt Ukraine plant after strikes
evidence: ArcelorMittal said on Friday it will halt operations at its Ukrainian plant after four missile strikes in five weeks killed five workers and injured 17, triggering a roughly $1 billion non-cash impairment charge.
The latest strike hit the plant on Sept. 21, following attacks on Aug. 17 and Sept. 14. One of the 17 injured employees remains in critical condition.
The company has provided more than $700 million to its Kryvyi Rih subsidiary since Russia's invasion of Ukraine began in February 2022.
ArcelorMittal said it was discussing the site's future with the Ukrainian government and would preserve the infrastructure to keep open the option of restarting production when conditions allow.

sources.title: Unions at Chile's Escondida mine reject bid to pause contract talks after worker's death
evidence: Unions at Chile's Escondida copper mine, the world's largest, pushed back on Friday after management sought to pause contract talks with unionized supervisors and staff following a fatal accident earlier this week.
The unions rejected the request, meaning talks will continue on schedule.
Unionized supervisors are due to vote from September 28 to September 30 on the company's latest contract offer.
Operations at Escondida, in Chile's northern Atacama Desert, were halted after the accident, then gradually resumed on Thursday while the causes remained under investigation.

sources.title: Brazil court blocks Braskem funding for Mexican unit's US bankruptcy plan
evidence: A Sao Paulo bankruptcy judge ordered Brazilian petrochemicals major Braskem to immediately halt payments and guarantees supporting the US Chapter 11 restructuring of its Mexican subsidiary, polyethylene (PE) producer Braskem Idesa.
The support package involves commitments worth about $800 million.
Braskem Idesa is a joint venture between Braskem (75% stake) and Mexico's Grupo Idesa (with the remaining 25%).
The judge also gave Braskem 15 days to file a detailed report on the operation's origin, consideration and impact.

sources.title: Ukraine says it struck Russian oil refinery as drone attacks intensify
evidence: Ukraine said it struck Russia's Ilsky oil refinery in the Black Sea region of Krasnodar overnight, setting the facility ablaze as both countries reported large-scale drone attacks, Bloomberg reported.
Three people were killed and two injured in the incident, according to the Krasnodar region's operational headquarters.
The Ilsky refinery is located about 850 kilometres southeast of Kyiv and has a design capacity of roughly 6.6 million tons annually.
Fuel supply disruptions have prompted Russian authorities to temporarily restrict most exports of gasoline, diesel and jet fuel.
